title: Role-structured relational graph with joint hand/handle motion diffusion
coverage_gap: Ten diagonal-cell demonstrations do not independently cover cabinet translation and yaw, nor recovery from missed contact. An action-only learner can memorize a reach/descend/pull script without representing when the handle actually follows the hand. A fitted hinge and fixed stage thresholds are additional assumptions that this candidate deliberately avoids.
reusable_regularity: Use hand, handle and goal as three role-labelled nodes with shared pairwise message functions. Nodes contain world positions, cabinet-canonical goal-relative positions, causal motion, gripper attributes and sign-invariant handle orientation/history. Directed edges carry both world and cabinet-relative position differences, relative motion and distance. Two shared residual message rounds form a 64-dimensional learned relational encoding, alongside 40 direct causal features. Jointly diffuse native world action4 followed by six cabinet-frame future hand/handle displacement channels. Predicting both moving entities should encourage distinguishing free hand movement from coupled pulling, without a hard-coded stage machine. The auxiliary channels are generated with the action by the common U-Net; they are never interpreted by a planner or a controller.
dependencies_preserved: Native world action coordinates are unchanged. The gripper is always the fourth native scalar, and fixed end-effector orientation is not treated as a rotatable translation.

Explicit world hand, handle and goal positions and cabinet yaw are present both through graph node attributes and a direct bypass. Cabinet-relative relations do not erase reachability, world cube saturation or fixed-finger alignment dependencies.

Current and previous gripper aperture, hand/handle finite differences and full handle orientation up to quaternion sign preserve causal contact and door motion information. Only the declared absent object2 zeros are omitted.

Door/cabinet dependencies are represented by observed handle pose, goal and cabinet yaw rather than hidden body poses or collision geometry. The design assumes this shared observation is sufficient; it obtains no simulator internals.

Message passing is per observation and both complete observations are returned to the common two-step conditioner. No future label, stage target, timestep-in-episode or valid mask enters condition or denoise.

evidence_refs.fact: The same ten complete current support episodes supply all supervision; there is no evaluation data in the bundle.
Native action4/world control, fixed orientation, handle geom center, current/previous state and observed cabinet yaw; factor coverage is only LL and HH.
Five demonstrations per training cell, saturated translation actions and constant +1 demonstrated gripper. The output gripper is nevertheless learned with the unmodified common action loss.

Early hand motion while the handle is static, then handle motion during pulling. Separate future hand and handle displacements can supervise this change in coupling without providing a phase label at deployment.
Different world positions and cabinet yaw produce another initial spatial relation under otherwise shared task semantics.
Hand remains by a handle on the opened door.
Another demonstration shows hand/handle interaction during visible door swing.
Another demonstration shows approach from above rather than straight displacement to the final goal.
Joint diffusion is allowed when encoded native action4 occupies the first four channels; future supervision is restricted to training_targets/diffusion_targets/training_loss.
The host fixes action epsilon weight 1 and mask.sum()*4 normalization, and inference initializes all joint channels from the host generator without labels.

expected_failure_signature: World actions require learning rather than enforcing the yaw dependence. Good C performance but failed contact/pull at extreme yaw would show that dual-frame features and relational weight sharing did not suffice for rotational extrapolation.

Auxiliary future motion can learn an optimistic handle trajectory from successful demonstrations. Repeated pulling with a stationary handle after missed contact would falsify the intended coupling benefit.

The larger joint denoising problem may hurt action fidelity under the fixed budget. Across-cell degradation rather than only OOD errors would indicate auxiliary competition/underfitting, not evidence that the task is nonrelational.

A three-node graph has no explicit moving obstacle mesh. Collision during descent despite accurate coarse hand/goal geometry would expose insufficient contact detail. All these outcomes are predicted, not measured.

required_runtime_fields.source: causal_context.raw_history [B,2,41]; inherited identity action mappings require no additional context
required_runtime_fields.action_frame: Identity native world xyz and gripper for encode/decode. Output first four joint channels only; no candidate clipping, action offsets, scaling, rollout, planning or auxiliary-based execution correction. The executor clips world action cube, applies native 0.01 m xyz scale and executes four of sixteen actions.
required_runtime_fields.inference_auxiliary: Six latent future displacement channels are jointly generated from diffusion noise. They never contain ground-truth future states at inference and are discarded by the executor.

training_only_targets.name: future_displacements
training_only_targets.source: Exact D_N obs[t+k+1,0:3] minus obs[t,0:3] and obs[t+k+1,4:7] minus obs[t,4:7], for k=0..15 with valid native actions. Both differences are rotated by observed cabinet yaw at chunk start t and divided by 0.1 m.
training_only_targets.padding: Unavailable tail entries are zero placeholders; auxiliary loss uses the same per-action valid mask, with its own six-channel denominator. The final obs[T] is used only as the valid outcome of action T-1.
training_only_targets.loss: Append six clean targets after action4, use the frozen joint diffusion noise process, and add 0.2 * sum(mask * squared_auxiliary_epsilon_error)/(6*mask.sum()). Denominator is clamped to at least one only for an all-invalid batch. The host's action4 epsilon loss remains unchanged, separately normalized and weight one.
training_only_targets.causality: The label array is returned from training_targets, not cached on the design. No support labels, masks or future frames are accepted by condition/denoise/identity decode. All modules are registered in build_modules and optimized only by the common joint loss.

support_fit: No fitted statistics or external weights. Fixed metric scales; future arrays exist only in the host training dataset. Deployment state is the inherited empty JSON object plus normal registered learned weights and role/adjacency buffers.
change_summary: Initial independent scientific design: learned role-shared relational message passing and joint state-action diffusion with identity native action frame. No fitted hinge, explicit stage gates or pretraining. No measured performance feedback has been used.
